about.title: Walnut Creek Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Five people died in Walnut Creek traffic in 2025, out of 310 injury collisions that left 413 people hurt. Whether the loss happened on Ygnacio Valley Road, along I-680, on N Main Street, or near Treat Boulevard, the questions afterward tend to be the same: who was responsible, what the family is owed, and how much time there is to act. California gives a spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in when no one in that first group exists. The claim is civil and moves on its own track, apart from any criminal case the Contra Costa County District Attorney may pursue. Most families have two years from the date of death to file, and considerably less when a public agency is involved. Our team handles wrongful death cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Walnut Creek Families Choose Us

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can sort out who in your family is eligible before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines Handled Early
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window shrinks sharply when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Getting our team engaged early protects that timeline.

items.title: Every Category of Loss Accounted For
items.desc: Recoverable losses go beyond funeral and burial costs to include the financial support your loved one would have provided and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. We document each of these so nothing is left out.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on I-680 near Walnut Creek and the driver was arrested. Do we have to wait for the criminal case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that runs separately from anything the district attorney does. You can move forward with the civil case regardless of whether criminal charges are filed, dropped, or still pending. Evidence from the criminal matter may help, but your family's two-year deadline keeps running either way.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring the claim?
items.answer: California puts the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children first in line. If there is no one in that group, certain financially dependent relatives and other heirs may have standing. We can review your specific family situation and explain who should be named.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a consultation?
items.answer: No. Our team provides free consultations. We work on contingency, meaning there is no attorney fee unless your family obtains a recovery. You can ask about how fees work before agreeing to anything.
